name: Data Compression and Storage Optimization
text:
# Data Compression and Storage Optimization

Also called: 3DGS Compression, Gaussian Quantization, Codebook-based Compression

## Overview
Data Compression and Storage Optimization addresses the excessive memory footprint and storage requirements of [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) scenes, which often exceed 1GB for real-world datasets due to per-Gaussian attributes [S1, S2, unofficial]. It reduces this footprint by replacing continuous per-Gaussian parameters with discrete codebooks, hash-based fields, or quantized representations, achieving [compression](#4-compression.md) ratios from 10× to over 25× while maintaining reconstruction quality [S1, S2, unofficial]. Unlike standard 3DGS, which treats each Gaussian as an independent primitive with full precision, these methods exploit spatial redundancy, sensitivity-aware clustering, or neural field approximations to share or compress attributes [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The family shares the goal of reducing the storage size of $N$ Gaussian primitives $\{G_i\}$, where each $G_i$ is defined by position $\mu_i$, scale $\hat{s}_i$, rotation $r_i$ (quaternion), opacity $o_i$, and spherical harmonic (SH) coefficients $c_i$ [S1, S2, unofficial].

1.  **[Codebook-Based Quantization](#11802-gaussian-parameter-compression-via-codebooks-and-adaptive-qu.md):** Most methods replace continuous attributes (typically [SH coefficients](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md) for color, and scale/rotation for geometry) with indices into a finite codebook $C$ [S1, S2, unofficial]. The storage cost shifts from $N \times D$ floats to $N \times \text{bits}(\text{index}) + |C| \times D$ floats, where $|C| \ll N$ [S1, unofficial].
2.  **Sensitivity-Awareness:** High-impact parameters are preserved in higher precision or excluded from aggressive clustering to prevent visual artifacts [S1, unofficial]. Sensitivity $S(p)$ is often defined as the gradient of the image energy with respect to the parameter, normalized by pixel count [S1, unofficial].
3.  **Spatial Redundancy:** Neighboring Gaussians often share similar geometric or color properties. Methods exploit this via shared neural fields ([hash grids](#936-hash-grids.md)) or clustering based on spatial coherence (e.g., Z-order/Morton order) [S1, S2, unofficial].
4.  **Quantization-Aware Training (QAT):** To recover quality lost during compression, [fine-tuning](#9138-fine-tuning.md) is performed where [quantization](#5935-quantization.md) is simulated during the forward pass but gradients are computed on continuous parameters during the backward pass [S1, S2, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [ASCII-Based Data Compression](11820-ascii-based-data-compression.md)
A method for optimizing data transmission speed during training by encoding numerical attributes into ASCII strings. It maps integers in $[0, 95]$ to ASCII characters 32–126 and floats to a base-94 integer character plus a delimiter `~` and decimal string. It yields modest speed improvements (~6%) but suffers from slow matrix traversal.

### [Sensitivity-Aware Vector Clustering](12167-sensitivity-aware-vector-clustering.md)
Reduces storage by clustering SH coefficients and shape parameters into codebooks using [sensitivity-aware k-means](#12167-sensitivity-aware-vector-clustering.md). It calculates sensitivity as the normalized gradient of image energy, excluding high-sensitivity vectors from clustering. It uses weighted distance $D(x, c_k) = S(x) \|x - c_k\|_2^2$ for centroid updates and applies entropy coding (DEFLATE) after Z-ordering.

### [Compact 3D Gaussian Representation (C3DGS)](12927-compact-3d-gaussian-representation-c3dgs.md)
Reduces memory by replacing per-Gaussian color with a shared hash-based neural field (Instant NGP) and geometry with a discrete codebook. It uses a learnable mask to prune redundant Gaussians and achieves over 25× compression. It exploits spatial redundancy by mapping positions to color features and quantizing scale/rotation.

### [Monte Carlo Specular Energy Aggregator](15439-monte-carlo-specular-energy-aggregator.md)
Compresses third-order SH to first-order SH by aggregating specular residuals via Monte Carlo sampling. It computes scalar energy magnitude $E_{mag}$ and directional tensor $E_{dir}$ from the residual between third- and second-order SH, then uses an MLP to predict first-order coefficients. It avoids pre-training distillation, unlike Mobile-GS.

### Sparse Adaptive Scalable Compact Gaussian Splatting
A compression method that utilizes vector clustering to encode color and geometric attributes into two codebooks, employing a sensitivity-aware k-means method to prioritize important parameters [S1, unofficial].

### 3DGS Quantization Compression
Reduces storage footprint by quantizing per-Gaussian attributes and using codebooks, achieving ~10× smaller sizes without significant quality loss [S2, unofficial]. The layout stores position in FP16, scales in FP16, opacity in INT8, and SH coefficients in INT8 or via codebooks [S2, unofficial].

## Background
3D Gaussian [Splatting](#23-splatting.md) was introduced by Kerbl et al. in 2023 [G]. The high storage cost of storing full SH coefficients and continuous parameters for millions of Gaussians led to immediate research into compression. Early methods like [LightGaussian](#8036-lightgaussian.md) combined pruning with INT8 quantization [S2, unofficial]. Subsequent works like C3DGS, SASCGS, and [EAGLES](#7990-eagles.md) explored [residual vector quantization](#12711-residual-vector-quantization-r-vq.md), sensitivity-aware clustering, and full [attribute quantization](#1912-attribute-quantization.md) to reduce scene sizes by 10× to 25× [S1, unofficial]. Recent approaches like MC-SEA focus on reducing SH order for mobile rendering without distillation [S1, unofficial].
